items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own theorem thm:NoUniversalSet at source lines 875-877: the set of all sets does not exist. The proof at source lines 879-883 is a short but genuinely two-step argument. It first argues by reductio from an assumed universal set V, and then it must pick the right axiom to apply: it uses Separation with V as the separating set, so that the Russell collection becomes a set, and it identifies that instance with the unrestricted Russell collection of all x with x not in x, which contradicts Russell's Paradox. The step that turns an unrestricted comprehension over the universe into an instance of Separation relative to V is the substance of the argument, and it is exactly the point the statement does not mention. No result outside the retained text is used.
